summary_paragraph: A male patient with a history of liver transplant, chronic kidney disease, and GERD was admitted for fever and confusion. He presented with a temperature of 102°F at home and was found to have elevated ammonia and mild leukocytosis. Initial evaluation included a spinal tap, imaging, and infectious workup, all of which were unremarkable except for a benign CSF and negative viral studies. He was treated with a dose of broad-spectrum antibiotics in the ED but showed no ongoing signs of infection. Lactulose was restarted for hepatic encephalopathy, and sirolimus was reduced to 2 mg daily to protect kidney function. The patient improved rapidly, remained afebrile, and was discharged home with instructions to continue lactulose, monitor mental status, and follow up with his primary and liver specialists.
